cards.text: That same day, right after the question about Caesar's coin, the Sadducees come to Jesus with a question of their own. It's like clearing out your inbox and hearing that DING before you even sit back down. And Matthew tells us one big thing about what these guys believe.

cards.question: Matthew says the Sadducees who come to Jesus believe the dead will rise again.

cards.text: They call Him Teacher, and then they bring up a rule from Moses. If a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow.

cards.question: In the rule from Moses the Sadducees quote, why does the brother marry the widow?

answers.text: To raise up children for his brother
To pay off his brother's debts
To look after his brother's flocks

cards.text: Then they tell Jesus about seven brothers among them. The first one marries and dies without having children, so he leaves his wife to his brother.

cards.question: In the Sadducees' story, the second brother has a child with the widow, and that's where it stops.

cards.text: Seven brothers. SEVEN. One wife. Friend, that's not a family story, that's a whole season of television. And last of all, the woman dies.

cards.question: Now the Sadducees ask Jesus their big question about the resurrection. What do they want to know about the woman?

answers.text: Whose wife she will be of the seven
Which brother she loved the most
Where her grave should be dug

cards.text: All seven were married to her, they say, so whose is she? Jesus doesn't tiptoe. He tells them flat out they're mistaken.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Sadducees they're mistaken. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They don't know the Scriptures or God's power
They counted the seven brothers twice
They brought their question on the Sabbath

cards.question: Jesus tells the Sadducees that in the resurrection, people will keep marrying just like they do now.
Jesus says that in the resurrection, people will be like the ___ in heaven.

cards.text: Then Jesus takes on the bigger question, whether the dead rise at all. He asks the Sadducees if they've never read what God said to them.

God said, "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob", and those are Israel's forefathers. Look at that little word "am," friend. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer being talked about in the past tense.

cards.question: Jesus says God is not the God of the ___, but of the ___.
When the crowds hear Jesus answer the Sadducees, how do they react?

answers.text: They are astonished at His teaching
They turn and walk away quietly
They ask Jesus to explain it again

cards.text: Question after question, all day long, and Jesus is still standing. Stick around, friend. This day's not done yet.

findings.problem: The card says this comes right after the question about Caesar's coin. That fact comes from the previous passage (Matthew 22:15-22), but the card only cites Matthew 22:23.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The Sadducees appear here for the first time, but the card never says who they are, such as a Jewish religious group. It only hints at what they believe, which card 2 asks about.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card cites only Matthew 22:27. Its "Seven brothers. SEVEN. One wife." line uses the seven brothers and the shared wife from Matthew 22:25-26, so the citation should start earlier.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Whose wife she will be of the seven," keeps the BSB's "of the seven" phrasing. That makes it sound more like the Bible than the plain wrong answers, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The first sentence ("All seven were married to her, they say, so whose is she?") repeats what card 8 just asked and answered. It recaps instead of moving the passage forward.
The wrong answer "They counted the seven brothers twice" is silly. It doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card calls Abraham, Isaac and Jacob Israel's forefathers. That fact comes from outside the passage and has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "Question after question, all day long" adds a time span. The text says only "That same day" (Matthew 22:23), not that the questions went on all day long.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
